newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver close lower on improved supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver close lower on improved supply.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carat closes 5.0 rupees lower at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes on dull demand It opened steady at 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) end 100 rupees lower at 56,200 rupees per piece.
** Silver (.999) finishes 30 rupees lower at 6,910 rupees per kg under the pressure of heavy arrivals of imported metals in the last last few days.
Standard gold 24 carats closed 5.0 rupees marginally lower at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes on improved arrivals. It opened steady at 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes.
"There has been a rise in imports in the wake of a recent fall in world prices. Supply has been more than demand," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lala Damani.
Damani said imports of gold into other centres such as Ahmedabad in western India and the capital city of New Delhi covering the northern region had been good.
"These centres are getting gold directly. It's not going from Bombay as in the past. So we have some excess gold," Damani said.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) lost 100 rupees to 56,200 rupees per piece due to subdued demand.
Silver (.999) lost 30 rupees to 6,910 rupees per kg with dealers reporting heavy arrivals in the market.
"At least 20 tonnes of silver must have arrived in the last three weeks," said a dealer.
Dealers said they expected the market to remain steady due to wedding season demand despite higher arrivals. (Conversion $1=35.76 rupees)
